newsitem.title: USA: Compaq settles packaging flap with states.
newsitem.headline: Compaq settles packaging flap with states.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp on Wednesday agreed to stop providing dealers with factory materials that could be used to repackage old computers and sell them as new, the Texas Attorney General said on Wednesday.

Following an industry-wide investigation, 22 state attorneys general alleged some independent computer dealers were deceiving customers by repackaging and selling as new computers that had been returned or repaired, Texas Attorney General Dan Morales said.
"Under the (settlement), Compaq will no longer provide dealers with factory marked boxes and sealing tape," Morales said in a statement announcing the settlement.

The Houston-based computer maker said the packaging had been provided to replace cartons that were scuffed or dented during shipment and dealers had been told not to repackage used computers for resale.

Compaq has ended links with one independent dealer recently for selling used machines as new, said Compaq attorney Bill Coston, a partner with law firm Venable, Baetjer, Howard and Civiletti in Washington, D.C.

"We have in fact stopped dealing with at least one company that wasn't handling its returns properly," he said. "They just were out-and-out selling used as new and we didn't facilitate it with packaging. We just found out they did it and said 'no more.'"
In the settlement, filed in a Dallas County, Texas district court, Compaq admitted no wrongdoing and agreed to pay $132,000 to the states to cover attorneys fees and investigative costs.

The Compaq settlement follows a September 5 agreement by Packard Bell Corp, which agreed to pay $1.5 million to settle allegations it sold as new computers that contained parts from previously sold computers and monitors.
Packard Bell said recycling components was a common practice in the computer industry and agreed to provide retailers with materials to inform consumers of the practice.
